chunks.subject: AP Chemistry
chunks.title: Q7 — Short Answer (4 points)
chunks.content: AP Chemistry Q7 (Short Answer), 4 points, one per part. Topic: glycolate ion (acid–base) and a reaction mechanism. A [Pt1]: circle a correct oxygen atom (either of the two equivalent resonance C–O bonds on the carboxylate is acceptable). B(i) [Pt2]: calculate Kb = [HAsc-analog][OH−]/[conjugate base] ≈ 6.8×10^−11 by substituting the correct concentrations. B(ii) [Pt3]: calculate Ka from Kw = Ka·Kb (Ka = 1.0×10^−14 / 6.8×10^−11 = 1.5×10^−4), consistent with B(i). C [Pt4]: agree that H3O+ acts as a catalyst — consumed in step 1 and regenerated in step 2, so it is not in the overall reaction. Common failure: circling a carbon rather than oxygen; using Ka = 1/Kb instead of Kw/Kb; agreeing in C without a mechanism-based justification.

chunks.subject: AP Chemistry
chunks.title: Q7 exemplar — Sample 7A, 4/4
chunks.content: Q7 scored 4/4. Circled a correct oxygen (A); correct Kb from substituting concentrations (B i); correct Ka via Kw = Ka·Kb (B ii); agreed on the catalyst, noting H3O+ is a reactant in step 1 and a product in step 2 and absent from the overall reaction (C). Full-credit model.

chunks.subject: AP Chemistry
chunks.title: Q7 exemplar — Sample 7B, 2/4
chunks.content: Q7 scored 2/4. Earned A (correct oxygen) and B(i) (correct Kb). Lost B(ii) (used Ka = 1/Kb instead of Kw/Kb) and C (agreed but gave no mechanism-based justification). Shows the common Ka–Kb relationship error.

chunks.subject: AP Chemistry
chunks.title: Q7 exemplar — Sample 7C, 1/4
chunks.content: Q7 scored 1/4. Earned only C (agreed and justified that H3O+ is consumed in step 1 and reappears as a product in step 2). Lost A (circled a carbon atom), B(i) (wrong glycolic-acid concentration and improper scientific notation), and B(ii) (set up a Ka expression but neither substituted concentrations nor used Kw/Kb). Illustrates a response holding only the catalyst identification.
